'''Radha Charan Gupta''' (14 August 1935 – 5 September 2024) was an Indian [[history of mathematics|historian of mathematics]], specialising in the history of [[Indian mathematics]].

== Life and career ==
Gupta was born on 14 August 1935 in [[Jhansi]], in what is now [[Uttar Pradesh]]. He attended secondary school in Jhansi, but there were few opportunities locally to pursue higher education, so he continued his education at the [[University of Lucknow]] with a merit scholarship. He married Savitri Devi in 1953, urged by his family to marry young so the [[dowry]] received could help pay his sister's dowry. He completed his bachelor's degree in 1955 and his master's degree in 1957.<ref name= ramasubramanian>{{cite book | last = Ramasubramanian | first = K. | editor-last = Ramasubramanian | editor-first = K. | chapter = Preface to the First Edition | pages = xiii–xviii | year = 2019 | title = Gaṇitānanda | publisher = Springer | doi = 10.1007/978-981-13-1229-8 | isbn = 978-981-13-1228-1 }}</ref>

To support his family, Gupta took a teaching job instead of immediately continuing doctoral studies.{{r|ramasubramanian}} He was a lecturer at [[Lucknow Christian College]] from 1957 to 1958. In 1958 he joined [[Birla Institute of Technology]] (BIT) in [[Ranchi]].{{r|scriba}}

In 1963 he read [[Bibhutibhushan Datta|Datta]] and [[Avadhesh Narayan Singh|Singh]]'s ''[[History of Hindu Mathematics]]'', became interested in the [[history of mathematics]], and got to know the mathematical historian [[T. A. Sarasvati Amma]]. She later supervised his Ph.D. at [[Ranchi University]], which he finished in 1971 with the dissertation ''Trigonometry in Ancient and Medieval India''.<ref name=IMU>[https://www.mathunion.org/ichm/prizes/kenneth-o-may/awarding-kenneth-o-may-prize-ivor-grattan-guinness-and-rhada-charan-gupta Awarding of the K.O. May Prize] from [[International Mathematical Union]]</ref>

Starting in 1979, he was in charge of BIT's Research Center for the History of Science.<ref name=scriba>{{cite journal |last=Scriba |first=Christoph J. |author-link=Christoph Scriba |year=1996 |title=A Birthday Tribute to R. C. Gupta |journal=Historia Mathematica |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=117–120 |doi=10.1006/hmat.1996.0014 }} Republished in {{cite book |editor-last=Ramasubramanian | editor-first=K. |pages=9–12 |year=2019 |title=Gaṇitānanda | publisher=Springer |doi=10.1007/978-981-13-1229-8_2 }}</ref> In 1982 he was awarded a full professorship at BIT, where he continued teaching until mandatory retirement in 1995.{{r|IMU}} After retiring, Gupta continued his research in mathematical history.<ref name=plofker>{{cite journal |last=Plofker |first=Kim |author-link=Kim Plofker |year=2009 |title=Professor R. C. Gupta Receives the Kenneth O. May Prize |journal=Gaṇita Bhāratī |volume=31 |number=1–2 |pages=115–118 }} Republished in  {{cite book |editor-last=Ramasubramanian | editor-first=K. |pages=13–15 |year=2019 |title=Gaṇitānanda | publisher=Springer |doi=10.1007/978-981-13-1229-8_3 }}</ref>

Gupta died in Jhansi on 5 September 2024, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[Amar Ujala]] |date=2024-09-05 |url=https://www.amarujala.com/uttar-pradesh/jhansi/padmashree-dr-radha-charan-gupta-an-internationally-renowned-mathematician-of-vedic-mathematics-passed-away-2024-09-05 |script-title=hi:Jhansi: पद्मश्री डॉ. राधाचरण गुप्ता का निधन, शिक्षक दिवस पर ली अंतिम सांस, उनके योगदान को रखा जाएगा जीवित |trans-title=Padma Shri Dr. Radha Charan Gupta passed away, breathed his last on Teacher's Day, his contribution will be kept alive |lang=hi |access-date=2024-09-10 }} {{pb}} {{cite news |newspaper=[[News18]] |date=2024-09-05 |title=Doyen of Vedic Mathematics Professor Radha Charan Gupta Dies, Bundelkhand University Mourns |url=https://www.news18.com/education-career/doyen-of-vedic-mathematics-professor-radha-charan-gupta-dies-bundelkhand-university-mourns-9041338.html |access-date=2024-09-10 }}</ref>

== Works ==
In 1969 Gupta addressed<ref>R.C Gupta (1969) "Second Order of Interpolation of Indian Mathematics", ''Indian Journal of History of Science'' 4: 92–94</ref> [[interpolation]] in [[Indian mathematics]]. He wrote on [[Govindasvamin]] and his interpolation of [[sine tables]]. Furthermore, he contributed an article on the work of [[Paramesvara]]: "Paramesvara's rule for the [[circumradius]] of a [[cyclic quadrilateral]]".<ref>R.C. Gupta (1977) [[Historia Mathematica]] 4(1): 67–74 {{doi|10.1016/0315-0860(77)90038-6}}</ref>

In 2019, a collection of Gupta's papers was published as a book:

* {{cite book
 | last = Gupta | first = Radha Charan
 | editor-last = Ramasubramanian | editor-first = K.
 | year = 2019
 | title = Gaṇitānanda: Selected Works of Radha Charan Gupta on History of Mathematics
 | publisher = Springer

 | isbn = 978-981-13-1228-1
 }}

== Awards and other professional activities ==
Gupta was one of the founders of the [[Indian Society for History of Mathematics]], and in 1979 was the founding editor of its journal, ''[[Gaṇita Bhāratī]]'', which he edited for over 25 years.<ref>{{cite book|last=Rajendra Bhatia|author-link=Rajendra Bhatia|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, v.I, Volume 1|year=2010|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9789814324359|page=42|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GFE1vx2pynMC&pg=42}}</ref>

In 1991 he was elected a Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], and in 1994 he became President of the Association of Mathematics Teachers of India.<ref name=IMU/> He became a corresponding member of the [[International Academy of the History of Science]] in February 1995.<ref>{{cite web|title=Radha-Charan Gupta|url=http://www.aihs-iahs.org/fr/node/528|publisher=[[International Academy of the History of Science]]}}</ref>

In 2009 he was awarded the [[Kenneth O. May Prize]] alongside the British mathematician [[Ivor Grattan-Guinness]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Indian professor wins prestigious mathematics prize |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/80128/indian-professor-wins-prestigious-mathematics.html |newspaper=[[Deccan Herald]] |date=2010-07-08 |access-date=2018-11-18 }} {{pb}} {{cite web |title=Radha Gupta Will Receive Kenneth O. May Prize at ICM 2010 |url=http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/?pa=mathNews&sa=view&newsId=896 |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=2010-07-12 |archive-date=2010-07-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100712205203/http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/?pa=mathNews&sa=view&newsId=896 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the first Indian to receive this prize.<ref>{{cite web |title=First Indian to get Prize in ICM2010 |url=http://www.icm2010.org.in/wp-content/icmfiles/uploads/RCGupta.pdf}}</ref>

In 2023, he was awarded the [[Padma Shri]] by the [[Government of India]] for his contributions in the field of literature and education.<ref>{{cite web |title=Padma Awards 2023 announced |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1893797 |website=Press Information Bureau |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt of India |access-date=2023-01-26 }}</ref>
